annotationRationale: The problem tests surface-area accounting for a composite solid. The alternative counts exposed surfaces directly and reveals why the upward-facing areas telescope to the largest square's area.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate. No area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The side lengths are 1 through 7, and the exposed area including the bottom is 658, choice B. Complete support of each smaller bottom face makes the answer independent of horizontal placement. No figure is required.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both useful distinct routes are retained: subtract contact areas, or count vertical and horizontal surfaces separately. Further reference variants add no necessary method.
review.annotationCheck: The composite-solid node covers identifying and using the cube components; cnm_p161 supplies the surface-area procedure. Cube roots appropriately support the setup. The second method also correctly identifies telescoping.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate. No area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The separate areas total 6(140)=840. Each of the six contacts removes two regions of the smaller face's area, totaling 2(91)=182. The bottom is retained, so the exposed area is 840-182=658.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The cited LIVE explanation and AoPS Solutions 2 and 6 support precisely this argument. Attribution and source-informed-original status are honest; the candidate explains contact regions in its own prose.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why subtraction fits. Counting both hidden regions at every contact prevents the main possible error, and the bottom-face convention is explicit.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h107 supports component decomposition, cnm_p161 supports cube surface areas, and cnm_076 supports recovering side lengths. The composite-solid node alone does not encode contact-area correction, but the written explanation supplies it.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native composite-solid, prism/cube surface-area and cube-root links are relevant. The task uses their component procedures rather than demonstrating every criterion of those topics.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 7.G.B.6 directly fits the composite-cube surface-area task. 8.EE.A.2 fits perfect-cube evaluation only. No nets are used, so 6.G.A.4 is not directly exercised. G-MG.A.1 offers limited shape-modeling overlap, not full coverage.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All immediate IDs are supported. The joint assessment concerns cube components and surface area; cube roots remain a setup skill.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The vertical faces contribute 4(140)=560. The exposed tops sum to 1+(4-1)+...+(49-36)=49, regardless of offsets. Every smaller bottom is covered, leaving only the largest bottom of area 49. The total is 658.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solutions 1 and 5 support the decomposition. The candidate independently explains cancellation and correctly includes the smallest cube's top, which the printed alternative sum in Solution 1 omits. The nonofficial source classification is correct.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The exposed-face categories are complete and disjoint. The top-area subtraction and cancellation are explained explicitly, including both surviving endpoints.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: The three geometric/setup IDs fit, and math:telescoping precisely matches the displayed consecutive differences and endpoint cancellation.
